# Prediction Market Oracle Research

Curated by Skill Harbor: a research workflow for treating prediction markets as data sources, forecasting inputs, or oracle-like signals for products, agents, dashboards, and corporate decision intelligence. Starts from the decision the signal is meant to inform, finds relevant markets and venues, records market-implied probabilities with timestamps and source links, then evaluates signal quality: liquidity, spread, market age, trader concentration, resolution authority, and geography restrictions. Compares against non-market sources such as filings, news, polls, and internal KPIs, and recommends whether the signal is usable, weak, or unsuitable for the stated decision. Covers integration patterns: research assistant context, dashboard signals, agent memory input, alerting, and scenario planning without automating trades. By @affaan-m, listed here with credit to its creator. From the affaan-m/ECC repository (MIT). Honest caveats: market prices are not objective truth; manipulation, thin liquidity, stale markets, and ambiguous outcomes must be called out. Informational inputs only, never investment advice. For on-chain or execution-linked systems, run llm-trading-agent-security (also listed here) before granting any write authority. Skill Harbor never reviews the code, review it yourself before use.
